name: Orrath Cardamom-Mango Stim Chews
description: Dense, slightly sticky chews delivering a calibrated low-dose stimulant payload via bioactive synth-compounds. Cardamom-mango flavor makes the functional bitterness palatable. Each chew is individually sealed in foil printed with a small dosage window.
flavor_profile: Warm spiced cardamom opening, ripe mango body, mild astringent finish from the stim-compound base — faint medicinal edge that regular users stop noticing
cultural_context: Positioned as the 'responsible' stim-candy for people who want the edge without the spike-and-crash of synthetic caffeine products. Popular with night-shift infrastructure workers, BCI-assisted data processors, and Tier 3 freelancers billing by the hour. Some users chew two at once despite the packaging warning, a habit the brand quietly benefits from.
story_hooks: Orrath's licensed bioactive compound has a narrow approval window — a regulatory review is coming up, and someone is paying to make sure the review goes badly.
A Tier 3 data processor has been chewing three packs a day for eight months; their BCI logs show something unusual building in their cognition metrics.
A counterfeit run of Orrath chews has hit the Shelf — same wrapper, wrong compound, wrong dose. People are getting sick.
